questions.prompt: What money is used in Turkey?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Turkey article.

questions.proof: The money of Turkey is called the Turkish Lira.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Ankara?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Turkey is Ankara.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Turkey?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Turkey article.

questions.proof: The capital city is Ankara, a city in the central region, called Anatolia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Turkey about 783,562 square kilometres; Norway about 385,207 square kilometres; Palestine about 6,020 square kilometres; Bahrain about 787 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Turkey?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Turkey on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Turkey article.

questions.proof: It shares borders with the Black Sea to the north; Georgia to the northeast; Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Iran to the east; Iraq to the southeast; Syria and the Mediterranean Sea to the south; the Aegean Sea to the west; and Greece and Bulgaria to the northwest.
